detail.body:
# ZeRO-3: reuse the weight partition as the master copy when it already has the master dtype

<!-- r3 2026-10-15, new PR. Branch peng-fix-zero3-master-copy-device-v1 (worktree
/fsx/peng/workspace/ds-fix-zero3-master-copy-device) on master 5f266e26d. Found 2026-10-03 in the MiniMax-M3 TP + EP
study (deepspeed-500b-study/minimax-m3-tp-ep/FINDINGS.md, item 7). Job IDs: SOURCES.md. -->

## Summary

`DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage3._create_fp32_partitions` reuses a sub-group's weight partition as its master copy when
the two would be identical (same dtype, on the device): under torch autocast with an fp32 model, and with bf16 master
weights. The check compares `tensor.device == self.device`, where `self.device` is a string such as `"cuda:0"`
(`get_accelerator().current_device_name()`). A `torch.device` never equals a string, so the branch never runs and
ZeRO-3 keeps a second copy of every partition: +4 bytes per parameter for an fp32 model under autocast, +2 with bf16
master weights. The fix compares with `torch.device(self.device)`.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and recent pull requests on 2026-10-15 ("master weights", "fp32 partition", "autocast", "stage3
device"): none touches this comparison.

## The change

`deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py`, one line:

```python
-                        self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[i].device == self.device:
+                        self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[i].device == torch.device(self.device):
```

The branch it enables already exists (the code comment above it explains it); offload, NVMe and the other
branches are unchanged.

## Measured

MiniMax-M3 built from its config (random weights), ZeRO-3, bf16 weights with bf16 master weights and Adam states, no
CPU offload. The fix was tested in a DeepSpeed study tree before this branch existed.

| Setup | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 node, 2 H200, first 4 layers, AutoEP 2, 4,096 tokens | 51.62 GiB allocated between steps, 62.04 GiB peak | 41.50 GiB allocated, 51.91 GiB peak; the same losses at every printed step (13.4375, 13.34375, 13.229167, 13.140625) |
| 4 nodes x 8 H200, all 60 layers (426B), AutoTP 4 x AutoEP 8, 8,192 tokens per GPU | out of memory in step 2 at 125.0 GiB allocated | trains: 117.9 GiB peak, 15.14 s per step (mean of steps 2-4) |
| the same at 16,384 tokens per GPU | | trains: 124.1 GiB peak, 25.17 s per step |

Runs with `"bf16": {"enabled": true}` and fp32 master weights are not affected: there the partitions are bf16 and
the master copy fp32, so the branch does not apply with or without the fix.

## Tests

`TestZero3AutocastSharesMasterWeights` (2 ranks, `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py`): torch autocast (bf16) without a
bf16 / fp16 section, so the model weights stay fp32; ZeRO-3 without offload. Every master partition must be the
weight partition itself (`master is model_partition`), then 2 training steps run.

Hardware: 1 node of 8 H200 (driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126, pytest 9.1.1.

```
# master 5f266e26d + only the new test: 1 failed, `assert master is model_partition`
# this branch:
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py::TestZero3AutocastSharesMasterWeights    # 1 passed
# the rest of the file on this branch:
pytest unit/v1/zero/test_zero.py                                          # 106 passed, 1 skipped (+ 1 failed: an
                                                                          # earlier version of the new test that
                                                                          # assumed fp32 partitions under bf16)
```

`pre-commit run --files` passes on both changed files.

## Compatibility

| Cell | Validated |
|---|---|
| ZeRO-3, no offload, fp32 model under torch autocast | yes (test) |
| ZeRO-3, bf16 master weights (AutoTP + AutoEP) | yes (1 node and 4 nodes, see Measured; before this branch existed) |
| ZeRO-3 with optimizer offload, NVMe | branch not reached (offload and NVMe branches come first) |
| ZeRO-1 / ZeRO-2 | not touched |
| Accelerators other than CUDA | `torch.device(name)` accepts every accelerator's device name; not run |

## AI assistance

This change, its test and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

+                        self.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[i].device == torch.device(self.device):
                     # When torch autocast is enabled, weights in the provided model (and thus groups in the so-called

@@ -1919,6 +1919,52 @@ def test(self, force_ds_optim):
             model, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, optimizer=optimizer, config=config_dict)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not get_accelerator().is_bf16_supported(), reason="bf16 is not supported on this accelerator")
+class TestZero3AutocastSharesMasterWeights(DistributedTest):
+    """With torch autocast and no bf16 / fp16 section, the model keeps its weights in float32, the master dtype, so
+    ZeRO-3 without optimizer offload must use each partition as its own master copy (_create_fp32_partitions) instead
+    of keeping a second float32 copy. The check compares the partition's torch.device with the optimizer's device
+    name. (With "bf16": {"enabled": true} as well, the partitions are bf16 and this branch is not taken.)"""
+    world_size = 2
+
+    def test(self):
+        hidden_dim = 64
+        config_dict = {
+            "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 2,
+            "optimizer": {
+                "type": "Adam",
+                "params": {
+                    "lr": 1e-3
+                }
+            },
+            "torch_autocast": {
+                "enabled": True,
+                "dtype": "bfloat16"
+            },
+            "zero_optimization": {
+                "stage": 3
+            },
+        }
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = SimpleModel(hidden_dim, nlayers=2)
+        model, _, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=config_dict)
+        optimizer = model.optimizer
+        partitions = [p for p in optimizer.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat if p is not None]
+        assert partitions and all(p.dtype == torch.float32 for p in partitions)
+        for model_partition, master in zip(optimizer.fp16_partitioned_groups_flat,
+                                           optimizer.fp32_partitioned_groups_flat):
+            assert master is model_partition
+        data_loader = random_dataloader(model=model,
+                                        total_samples=4,
+                                        hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
+                                        device=model.device,
+                                        dtype=torch.float32)
+        for batch in data_loader:
+            loss = model(batch[0], batch[1])
+            model.backward(loss)
+            model.step()
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("training", [True, False])
 class TestZeroPartitionCache(DistributedTest):
     world_size = 1

reviews.body:
The fix itself is right: `torch.device == str` was always False, so the alias branch was dead. But that dead branch was also what kept hp and lp storage separate everywhere, and `offload_states` / `reload_states` rely on that. Turning it on breaks the offload round trip, and it now also fires for plain fp32 ZeRO-3, not only autocast / bf16-master runs.

**1. [blocking] `offload_states` / `reload_states` desync the weights once the partitions alias** — [`stage3.py:1162`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/1409708dc4688bea5f035c1de545f365132225b7/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L1162), [`stage3.py:3881`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/1409708dc4688bea5f035c1de545f365132225b7/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L3881), [`stage3.py:3948`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/1409708dc4688bea5f035c1de545f365132225b7/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L3948)

Once `fp32_partitioned_groups_flat[i] is fp16_partitioned_groups_flat[i]`, offloading `hp_params` rebinds `.data` of the shared tensor while the `ds_tensor`s still point into `lp_param_buffer`. After the next `step()` they get repointed to the new storage, `lp_param_buffer` goes stale, and a later `lp_params` offload/reload restores stale weights.

Repro on the CPU accelerator (1 rank, plain fp32 `nn.Sequential`, Adam, ZeRO-3, no optimizer offload): step → offload/reload `[hp_params]` → step → offload/reload `[lp_params]`. On this branch the module weights change by up to 1e-2 across the `lp_params` round trip and no longer share storage with `lp_param_buffer`; on the merge base the same sequence is exact.

Also, while aliased, offloading `lp_params` can't free device memory (the master still references the old storage), and after a reload the two lists are separate tensors again, so the saving silently disappears. `TestDynamicOffloadStatesZero3` only runs bf16, where nothing aliases, so it doesn't catch this. Suggest moving hp and lp together for aliased groups (and re-aliasing after reload), plus an fp32 / autocast parametrization of that test.

**2. [should-fix] This now applies to every plain fp32 ZeRO-3 run** — [`stage3.py:1162`](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/1409708dc4688bea5f035c1de545f365132225b7/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage3.py#L1162)

The branch also fires without any bf16 / fp16 / autocast section, but the summary lists only autocast with an fp32 model and bf16 master weights, so reviewers may read plain fp32 runs as untouched. Please call that out, and add a numerical parity test (aliased vs. a forced copy over a few steps) in addition to the identity check in `TestZero3AutocastSharesMasterWeights`.

**3. [question] `GatheredParameters` edits now persist in fp32 runs**

With the alias, weight edits under `GatheredParameters(..., modifier_rank=0)` now go straight into the master copy in fp32 runs. On master the next `step()` overwrote them unless `refresh_fp32_params()` was called (in my check the weight mean is -0.011 on master vs. 0.500 kept here); bf16 runs keep the old behaviour. Is that intended? If so it deserves a note. Related: with #8843 the fp32 sub-groups from `keep_in_fp32_modules` will alias too, and #8843 still allows `hp_params` offload for mixed dtypes, which is the half that breaks the alias.
